nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
START HERE - JOY-LTX 2.5 TAKE (one prompt, one take, one generation)

1. SCENE IDEA: type your premise.
2. Writer: pick a model you have (a hosted/cloud model writes best).
3. MASTER CONTROLS: render size (960x544 ships), take_seconds (8), upscale = auto. Auto plans for YOUR card and prints it: x2 -> 1920x1088 when it fits, else x1.5 -> 1440x832, else one pass at the render size. Want it anyway? Set x2 / x1.5 by hand (it will stream or run out of VRAM - your call), or type a bigger vram_gb.
4. USE I2V (optional): load a picture, flip the gate on -> the take starts from that frame. Off = text-to-video.
5. Run. One video with sound.

Sizes that fit: 24 GB = 8 s at x2, ~12 s at x1.5, 30 s single pass. 32 GB = 12 s at x1.5, 30 s single pass at 1280x736.
The writer writes one continuous speech in beats (beat_seconds); the SCRIPT node folds them into one LTX prompt. Read-me note: models + links.

nodes.title: WRITER
widgets_values:
THE WRITER

long_story + join style "extend take": one continuous speech in beats sized by MASTER CONTROLS. The SCRIPT node folds the beats into a single LTX prompt.
Cloud model returned 503 / empty? Pick another model in the list and Run again.
No writer? mode = passthrough and type your own paragraph in the story box.

nodes.title: negative
widgets_values: pc game, console game, video game, cartoon, childish, ugly

nodes.title: ENGINE - LTX-2.5 two-pass
widgets_values:
ENGINE: LTX-2.5, one or two passes.

Pass 1 at the planned size (8 distilled steps). When MASTER CONTROLS says two_pass: latent upscale (x2 or x1.5 - the switch picks the file) then pass 2 refines (3 steps); off = pass 2 never runs. Everything ships at the verified values; you normally touch only the DiT file (your tier) and the encoder file. Out of VRAM? smaller size or fewer seconds - or accept the streaming and wait.

nodes.title: SCENE IDEA (your premise)
widgets_values: A woman in her thirties with dark hair tied back, wearing a rust-orange sweater, sits at a kitchen table with a mug of coffee going cold and talks straight through, without stopping, about the night the power went out on her whole street and her house was the only one whose lights stayed on. Dry, matter-of-fact, American. One continuous take, static medium close-up, warm tungsten kitchen.

nodes.title: REWRITER (story -> chained shot prompts)

je_widget_values.story_idea: Two people talk across a booth in a late-night roadside diner about an impossible power outage: the whole street went dark for six minutes but her repair shop kept running, its lights got brighter, and the meter outside ran backwards. He is a sceptical man in his fifties in a faded blue mechanic's jacket; she is a woman in her late twenties in an oversized cream sweater and round wire-frame glasses. One warm pendant lamp above the table is the only light, rain on the window behind them, static camera at the end of the table holding both of them in a two-shot the whole time. Four shots, one continuous conversation, no camera cuts.

nodes.title: SCRIPT -> one LTX prompt (from the writer)
widgets_values:
A static camera on a desk tripod frames him from the chest up, centred, and the framing never changes for the whole take. Live-action footage, shallow depth of field, fine 35mm grain. A man in his forties with a shaved head and a full dark beard, wearing a plain charcoal t-shirt, sits in a mesh office chair at a home desk against a flat beige wall. Soft daylight from a window off camera-left is the only light. He speaks American English in a level, unhurried register. He rests both forearms on the desk and looks into the lens, and the man in the charcoal t-shirt says, "This workflow runs two engines. The script is the same either way." He raises his eyebrows once.

Soft daylight from a window off camera-left is the only light. He speaks American English in a level, unhurried register. He sits exactly as he was, both forearms on the desk, and the man in the charcoal t-shirt says, "H3 chains the shots. Two point five does them in one pass and finds its own cuts." He turns one hand palm-up.

nodes.title: JOY-LTX 2.5 - read me
widgets_values:
## Joy-LTX 2.5 - JoyAI-Echo's performance on LTX-2.5

**DiT file** (models/diffusion_models): pick by card and GPU family. Both doses in every tier: **070T30** (default) / **100T50** (livelier; same links with `100T50` in the name).
- 16 GB: [Q4_K_S.gguf](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-gguf/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-Q4_K_S.gguf) (RTX 30/40) · [comfy-w4a8](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-comfy-native/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-comfy-w4a8.safetensors) or [comfy-nvfp4](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-comfy-native/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-comfy-nvfp4.safetensors) (RTX 50) · 12 GB: [Q3_K_M.gguf](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-gguf/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-Q3_K_M.gguf)
- 24 GB: [Q5_K_M.gguf](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-gguf/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-Q5_K_M.gguf) (RTX 30/40, the default) · [Q6_K.gguf](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-gguf/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-Q6_K.gguf) · [comfy-mix4x8-17.0GB](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-comfy-native/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-comfy-mix4x8-17.0GB.safetensors) (RTX 50)
- 32 GB: [comfy-int8](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-comfy-native/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-comfy-int8.safetensors) (fastest on RTX 50) · [Q8_0.gguf](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-gguf/blob/main/LTX25dist-echoVid-070T30-v2-DiT-Q8_0.gguf)
The canvas loader (**JoyLTX Load Model**) takes either family; `.gguf` needs **ComfyUI-GGUF** installed. RTX 30/40 = GGUF, RTX 50 = comfy-native.
All files: [GGUF repo](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-gguf) · [comfy-native repo](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-comfy-native) · [dev merges](https://huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-dev) (bf16/fp8/int8, add your own distill LoRA) · Civitai: **Joy-LTX 2.5**.

**Also needed** (Lightricks/LTX-2.5 on Hugging Face): `ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16` + `ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16` -> models/vae · `ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0` -> models/latent_upscale_models (optional for 24 GB: `ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x1.5-1.0` from LTX-2.3) · text encoder `gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot` -> models/text_encoders (16 GB: the 10.6 GB `gemma4-12b-ltx25-comfy-w4a8` from LTX-2.5-Quantized).

**Writer**: `writer_pack/ComfyUI_JoyAI_Echo_GGUF_Nodes` from this zip -> custom_nodes (our writing rules are inside; the Manager copy lacks them). Point it at an Ollama with a cloud model, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

**Speed**: on RTX 50 add `--enable-triton-backend` to the launch line for comfy-native files (about 2x). GGUF is unaffected.

Models: huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-gguf · huggingface.co/joeygambino/joyai-echo-ltx25-echoVid-comfy-native
Nodes + canvases: github.com/jlucasmcrell/ComfyUI-JoyLTX25

PLUS LANES

LoRA stack - up to four LoRAs on the DiT; (none) or strength 0 = skipped. On a DEV merge, the official LTX-2.5 distilled LoRA at 0.4-0.6 is what makes it few-step.

REFS BY NAME - cast a character from a folder. Photos in ComfyUI/input/joyecho_refs/<name>/; the node reads the script, finds the named character, and keyframes attaches their photo at frame 0 (ref_strength 0.5) - the person in the photo is the person in the take, framing stays free. Use portraits, not busy scene photos.

save audio - the finished soundtrack as flac next to the video.
